title: The hunter on the mountain
hookLine: Arjuna fights a rough mountain hunter and loses, and the hunter turns out to be Shiva
carry: shiva lives in everyone, even the hunter

cards: High in the Himalaya, Arjuna is fasting and praying for weapons before the great war. A boar comes charging at him. He shoots, and at the same moment so does a hunter, a rough mountain man, with a woman at his side.
Two arrows, one boar. Whose kill is it? They quarrel.
Arjuna, the finest archer alive, starts shooting at the hunter, and his arrows simply vanish into him. His quiver runs empty. He swings his bow, and the hunter snatches it away.
They wrestle, and the hero of the Mahabharata is crushed to the ground by a stranger from the hills.

teach.h: THE GARLAND IS ON THE HUNTER'S HEAD.
teach.b: Beaten, Arjuna does the one thing left. He makes a small altar of earth, honors Shiva there, and lays a garland of flowers on it. Then he looks up.
The garland is on the hunter's head.
The hunter was Shiva all along, and the woman beside him was the Goddess, Uma. Arjuna falls at his feet, and Shiva, pleased with his courage, gives him the great weapon he came for.
The Mahabharata story says what an old hymn says too.

teach.h: THE RUDRAM BOWS TO HIM IN EVERYONE.
teach.b: The Shri Rudram, in the Krishna Yajur Veda, bows to Rudra, the fierce form of Shiva, over and over, and in places you wouldn't expect: in hunters, potters, carpenters, chariot makers, in forests, fields and streams.
It even names the lord of thieves.

teach.h: NAMAH SHIVAYA: I BOW TO SHIVA.
teach.b: Inside it are the words that became a well-known mantra: namah shivaya, I bow to Shiva, a name that means the kind one, the auspicious one.
Om namah shivaya. This is a core Hindu teaching, and Shaivas, the Hindus who worship Shiva as the highest, hold it especially close: the Lord isn't only in the temple.
He fills the whole world, and he can turn up as the rough stranger you'd never have guessed. At a kirtan the line goes out fast and comes back slower, round after round.
Each round can be a bow to someone different: the person beside you, the one singing off-key, the one you'd rather not sit near. Arjuna learned it flat on the ground; the kirtan teaches it gently.

how: At a kirtan, om namah shivaya is sung as a simple call-and-response line, often slowing over many rounds; Shaiva Hindus also repeat it as a mantra in daily japa.

o: the order of rites a priest follows at a temple
the songs a group sings by heart, like om namah shivaya

games.q: the hunter and the hymn — tap the pairs.
p: bows to Shiva in potters and hunters

s: Arjuna beat the hunter in the end
the hunter overpowered him; only when his garland for Shiva turned up on the hunter's head did Arjuna see who it was.
the Rudram bows to Shiva in the potter and the carpenter
it bows to Shiva in hunters, potters, carpenters, forests, fields and water, and even names the lord of thieves.
only Shaivas ever sing this line
Shaivas hold it close, but people from other Hindu homes sing it at kirtan too.

games.q: you're Arjuna. a rough stranger has beaten you, and now your garland for Shiva is on his head. what do you do?
o: fall at his feet: the Lord was in the hunter all along.
walk off and look for a proper temple.
games.why: Arjuna bowed, and Shiva gave him the weapon he came for. the Rudram bows the same way: to Shiva in hunters, potters, carpenters, everyone.

practice: Let the hands rest and the jaw loosen, and on the out-breath say the line silently, or aloud if you're alone: om namah shivaya.
Each round, bow inwardly to one person: someone you love, then someone you barely notice, then someone you find hard, the way Arjuna finally bowed to the hunter.
If you pray, let the line be your prayer; if not, let it be a way of seeing each one as more than you'd guessed.

wordCard.voice: Kirtan repertoire. Today's song: om namah shivaya, I bow to Shiva, the Lord the Rudram finds in everyone, even a hunter on a mountain.

orig.note: Sanskrit, in Devanagari: namah shivaya, I bow to Shiva. The words appear in the Shri Rudram.

carryVoice: Your line: shiva lives in everyone, even the hunter. Om namah shivaya, a bow to each one. Until tomorrow.
